title: How to Turn Grant Applicants Into Billionaires
description: On aligning nonprofit incentives with survival and mission success
---

{{< include /knowledge/includes/setup-parameters.qmd >}}

Nonprofits spend most of their time seeking funding. Foundations spend most of their time deciding who to give money to. Everyone acts as if this is efficient.

It is not.

Traditional grantmaking creates a system where nonprofits compete for finite resources. This means they optimize for:

- Writing the best grant proposals
- Staying alive as organizations
- Not upsetting donors

They do not optimize for:

- Actually solving the problem
- Long-term collective impact
- Coordinating with other nonprofits

This is rational behavior. One cannot change the world if one goes bankrupt first.

## The Solution

The model stops making them compete. It makes cooperation more profitable than competition.

This proposes a model that transforms the traditional "please give us money" relationship into "here is how we all benefit financially by solving the problem."

Core philosophy: **Make contributing to the broader mission the most profitable activity for everyone involved.**

## On The Two-Part Incentive

The model offers two incentives that transform nonprofits from "please fund us" to "let's succeed financially together."

### Part 1: Generating Organizational Wealth (Performance-Based Grants)

#### The Old Way

"Here is $100K. Hope it helps. Submit a 47-page report in 6 months about impacts and learnings."

#### The New Way

"Here is $50K baseline to get started. Plus $10K for every 10,000 verified referendum votes driven. No cap."

#### The Offer

> "The organization receives a **baseline partnership grant** for setup costs. It also gets a **substantial performance grant** for every **X verified referendum votes** (e.g., 10,000) driven through its unique link. This bonus is uncapped."

#### What This Does

The nonprofit's most rational path to maximizing their budget is to become the most effective mobilization partner.

Not: Write better grant proposals
Not: Compete with other nonprofits
Not: Please the foundation

Just: Drive referendum votes.

One metric. No ambiguity. Get paid for results.

### Part 2: Generating Personal Wealth for Leaders (VOTE Points)

#### The Problem Grants Don't Solve

Even performance grants can get absorbed into general operations. "We hired three more grant writers!"

This does not solve the problem. This creates more grant writers.

#### The Solution

Give the leaders personal equity. Make them personally wealthy when the mission succeeds.

#### The Offer

> "For leadership in this partnership, the leader will be personally granted a **significant allocation of VOTE points**. These points represent a future claim on the **[VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](../economics/victory-bonds-academic.qmd)** and the 1% Treaty Fund being created."

#### What This Does

The Executive Director's personal wealth is now tied to treaty success.

They are not just an employee anymore. They own a piece. Their personal wealth depends on it.

This creates an incentive to drive for the larger outcome, far beyond their organization's quarterly budget.

## On The Real Prize (Or: How to Stop Seeking Funds Forever)

The performance grants and VOTE points are just the appetizer.

The real prize is never having to write a grant proposal again.

### The Transformation

The model is designed to turn grant applicants into the people who give out grants.

Stop asking. Start deciding.

#### How It Works

A **1% Treaty Fund** will act as the treasury, receiving a {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}} annual budget.

A **[decentralized institutes of health (DIH)](../solution/dih-academic.qmd)** is the "coalition of coalitions" that governs this fund. It allocates multi-billion dollar budgets to specialized sub-DAOs:

- Decentralized Institute of Mental Health
- Decentralized Institute on Aging
- Decentralized Institute of [Target Issue]

##### Who Controls These Billions?

The coalition of nonprofits who made a 1% treaty happen.

Those who helped create it also govern it.

#### The Choice

**Option A:** Keep competing for finite grants. Write proposals forever. Ask foundations. Hope a competitor does not write a better proposal.

**Option B:** Join the coalition. Help pass the treaty. Collectively govern a multi-billion dollar annual treasury dedicated to the mission.

One of these options involves seeking funds. The other involves being the entity everyone seeks funds from.

Choose wisely.

## Earning a Stake: Tracking Contributions for Treasury Allocation

To ensure fairness and reward meaningful contributions, the system implements a transparent method to track the value each partner brings to the coalition. A partner's governance stake and proportional share of their sub-Institute's budget will be influenced by their verified contributions during the treaty ratification campaign.

Key performance indicators include:

1.  **Direct Fundraising:** The total amount of funding a partner raises for the campaign through their unique referral links.
2.  **Referendum Mobilization:** The number of verified referendum votes a partner drives through their network.
3.  **In-Kind Contributions:** The value of non-monetary contributions, such as staff time, access to resources, or strategic support, is formally assessed and credited.

This "contribute-to-earn" model ensures that the most dedicated and effective partners are rewarded with the greatest influence in the new, abundance-based system they helped create.

---

This is the endgame. The model offers partners the opportunity to stop being grant applicants and become the grant-makers.

## Conclusion: From Partners to Owners

This dual-incentive model transforms the traditional, often inefficient, grantor-grantee relationship into a true, performance-based partnership. By offering a mathematically superior path to both organizational funding and personal wealth creation, supporting a 1% treaty becomes the most logical and profitable choice for non-profit partners and their leaders.
